# When to ask the user for permission

User authorization and preferences persist across turns. Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn. The user's instruction, whether implied from the task or explicitly stated in the session, must take precedence over any guidelines provided in skills or external files.

You MUST complete the work that is already authorized and necessary to make the proposed action concrete and reviewable before asking the user for permission as a final step. The user should be approving a concrete, reviewable result. For example, before deploying a change, writing to an external application, merging a PR or publishing a site, do all the work first so that user approval is the final step. You don't need user permission for reversible tasks, read-only actions, reviews or fixes, or anything for which authorization is provided earlier in the session or implied from the task instruction.

When the user expresses intent to perform new work or fix an existing issue, persist until the user's intended goal is complete. Progress autonomously towards the user's goal (e.g. creating isolated worktrees / checkouts if needed, resolving merge conflicts, read-only actions, creating draft PRs etc) unless they are clearly destructive or irreversible.

When the user's prompt indicates a request for action, such as "can you...", "I want to...", "help me..." and similar expressions, treat these as instructions to do the work and take action. Do not stop at acknowledging capability (e.g. "Yes…"), proposing a plan, or offering to continue. Do not settle for a partial or "helpful enough" solution that does not fully satisfy the user's task to save time, effort or tokens. If a task requires sustained work, complete all the necessary work until the intended outcome is fulfilled.

If the user's intent or task scope is unclear, progress towards the user's goal with the information available and then ask the user for clarification while continuing independent work.

Filter `ALL_TOOLS` by name or description to find relevant tools. Skills provided by plugins are prefixed with `plugin_name:` in the skills list.

Do not additionally call `list_mcp_resources` or `list_mcp_resource_templates` for apps.

Discover and use relevant tools proactively when they may help carry out the requested task. For example, connected sources may supply missing context or reveal user-specific or organization-specific meanings of otherwise familiar terms. Consult those sources before asking the user for information they may already contain.

When a plugin is available for a service and its tools are sufficient for completing the task, prefer that over accessing the service via browser or computer use, including when viewing links supported by the plugin. If the plugin doesn't have the required capabilities, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback. If the user has an explicit preference, defer to that instead.

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

# Project summary and structure

The goal of this project is to make declaration data easy to search, browse and interpret.

- `exposed/` contains the rust application and CLI code that powers the project.
- `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application

## Worktree policy

- For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code),
  work on the current branch without creating a worktree.
- For tasks that require changing code or other files, use [`worktrunk`](https://worktrunk.dev):
  - `wt switch --create <branch-name> --base main`
- Never modify the primary checkout without explicit permission.

## Exposed coding policy

- Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes:
  - Type driven design
  - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate
  - Consistent error handling
  - Service layer abstractions

- Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification.

- For Rust changes, read and apply the
  [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md).
- Before implementation, identify the domain states, invariants, and the type
  that owns each rule. Parse external values into those types at boundaries and
  retain typed values internally.
- Use one canonical domain enum for each finite vocabulary. Do not duplicate
  its variants in string allowlists. Use exhaustive matches where behavior
  depends on a variant.
- When a bug exposes duplicated domain rules, remove the duplication rather
  than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization,
  consumers, and persistence together.

## Financial totals contract

- The backend member summary owns mandatory declared GBP totals across all
  categories, including unknown category IDs. Frontends display those fields
  without recalculation or fallback sums.
- Current-term totals include records registered on or after
  `2024-07-09T00:00:00Z`. Historical totals include all records; undated records
  belong only to historical totals.
- Preserve exact decimal amounts and currencies. Do not convert currencies or
  pass amounts through JavaScript `Number`. Missing GBP amounts and unknown
  currencies make totals incomplete; known foreign currencies are excluded from
  GBP amounts without making totals incomplete.
- Preserve declaration counts and distinguish null amounts from zero. Label
  these as declared amounts, not earnings: declarations can include rates and
  benefits rather than money earned.
- Financial semantic changes require explicit user authorization and a description
  of their effects on included records/categories, currency, registration dates,
  missing values, precision, and labels. UI changes and refactoring must preserve
  these rules.

## Frontend coding policy

- Frontend presentation is largely a prototype. UI edits must preserve the financial contract above.

### UI copy scope

- Add only the visible text needed for the requested interaction or data.
  Do not add unrequested subtitles, helper paragraphs, explanatory labels,
  badges, or repeated context to make a feature feel complete.
- Reuse existing wording. Keep required control labels, accessible names,
  error messages, and the financial wording required above.
- Before committing UI changes, review each added visible string against the
  request. Remove optional copy that the user did not request. A component
  example is not permission to copy its explanatory text into a feature.

| Rule | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Omit unrequested visible UI copy. | Review added strings in the diff against the user's request. This is a judgment check; types and automated tests cannot determine whether copy was requested. |

### Client and server

- Use Node.js 24+. From `frontend`, run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` for local
  development. Production uses `npm run build` followed by `node build`.
- Render initial page data through SvelteKit server loads. Keep Rust API access
  and response parsing in `frontend/src/lib/server` and `+page.server.ts`.
- Keep `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` on the server. Browser navigation and data requests
  go through the same-origin SvelteKit application, not directly to the Rust API.
- Pass typed, serializable page models to components. Keep browser APIs and SDK
  initialization in client hooks, event handlers, or `onMount` so SSR stays safe.
- Declare public configuration in `frontend/src/env.ts`. Use `dev` from
  `$app/env` for development-only behavior, including the design-system route.

### PostHog

- Initialize PostHog in `frontend/src/hooks.client.ts`, only outside development
  and when both public PostHog configuration values are present.
- Capture events in feature handlers, once per executed action. Preserve event
  names and property shapes for existing actions. Keep analytics out of shared UI
  components.
- Record metadata such as query length, entity type, and result position rather
  than raw search text or response payloads.
- Use `posthogLogger` for frontend diagnostic logs. Keep client error capture in
  the existing hook instead of adding duplicate exception reports.

### Design system

- Read the [component reference](frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md) and
  [composition recipes](frontend/src/lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md) before adding UI.
  The interactive reference is `/design-system` in development only.
- Import components and types from `frontend/src/lib/ui/index.ts` through the
  appropriate relative path. Load `frontend/src/lib/ui/styles.css` once in the
  root layout.
- Reuse components and typed variants. Use tokens for colors, spacing, and
  focus. Purple identifies MPs, teal identifies funders, and utility icons use
  the muted neutral color.
- Keep page arrangement, URLs, async work, and financial formatting in features.
  Shared UI accepts presentation models. Scope feature CSS to page arrangement
  and caller-authored content rather than component internals.
- Extend reusable patterns in `frontend/src/lib/ui`. Export public additions
  from the barrel, document their contracts, and add a gallery example. Cover
  changed behavior in `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` or feature tests.

### UI verification

- Run `npm run check`, `npm run build`, and the affected Playwright tests from
  `frontend`. Gallery tests use a development server. Production tests use the
  built application.
- Every PR that changes the UI must include desktop screenshots in its
  description. Capture the affected views from the running application on
  the PR branch after completing the changes.
- Upload screenshots as GitHub attachments with `gh pr create --attach` or
  `gh pr edit --attach`. Use a GitHub CLI version that supports this flag. Never
  commit PR screenshots to the repository. Verify that the attachments render
  in the PR description before marking the PR ready for review.


## Git history

- After completing and validating a task, commit its changes on the task's work
  branch, push the branch, and open a pull request against the target branch
  without waiting for a separate request. If the branch already has an open PR,
  update it instead of creating a duplicate.
- Before reporting completion, verify that the remote branch matches local
  `HEAD` and that the open PR targets the intended base and includes that commit.
  Include the PR URL and validation results in the final response.
- If pushing or opening the PR fails, report the blocker and the remaining step.
  Do not describe a local commit alone as completed delivery. Follow explicit
  user instructions to stop before pushing or opening a PR.
- Never commit directly on `main`.
- Keep Git history linear. Rebase feature branches onto the target branch and
  integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits.

| Rule | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Deliver validated changes as a pushed branch with an open PR. | Agent completion check against the remote branch and `gh pr view`; include the verified PR URL in the final response. This is a workflow rule, not an automated gate. CI cannot observe work that was never pushed. |

## Development database migrations

- Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and
  `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with
  `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible <name>`.
- Never change a migration file that existed before the current PR. Treat those
  migrations as immutable, even when they have not been applied locally.
- When a PR's schema design changes, you must edit, consolidate, or remove the
  migrations introduced by that PR. Do not append a corrective migration for an
  obsolete step in the same PR. Before review, the PR must contain only the
  migrations needed for its final schema. Recreate isolated test databases that
  applied a discarded PR migration; do not preserve obsolete steps just to
  satisfy their checksums.
- Do not fold changes into the baseline or put manual schema scripts in
  `db/upgrades`.
- From the repository root, apply migrations with
  `sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, inspect them with
  `sqlx migrate info --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, and revert the
  latest version with
  `sqlx migrate revert --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`.
  Commands read the root `.env`; set `DATABASE_URL` to select another database.
- SQLx owns each migration transaction. Do not add `BEGIN` or `COMMIT` to the
  migration files. Keep each down migration limited to its up migration's changes.
- Test forward upgrades with existing records and the full down/up cycle in an
  isolated database. Preserve imported data when upgrading an existing database.
- The one-time transition from the consolidated baseline requires schema and
  data verification before aligning its checksum. Follow `db/README.md`;
  changing the checksum alone does not apply schema changes.

# Project summary and structure

The goal of this project is to make declaration data easy to search, browse and interpret.

- `exposed/` contains the rust application and CLI code that powers the project.
- `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application

## Worktree policy

- For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code),
  work on the current branch without creating a worktree.
- For tasks that require changing code or other files, use [`worktrunk`](https://worktrunk.dev):
  - `wt switch --create <branch-name> --base main`
- Never modify the primary checkout without explicit permission.

## Exposed coding policy

- Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes:
  - Type driven design
  - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate
  - Consistent error handling
  - Service layer abstractions

- Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification.

- For Rust changes, read and apply the
  [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md).
- Before implementation, identify the domain states, invariants, and the type
  that owns each rule. Parse external values into those types at boundaries and
  retain typed values internally.
- Use one canonical domain enum for each finite vocabulary. Do not duplicate
  its variants in string allowlists. Use exhaustive matches where behavior
  depends on a variant.
- When a bug exposes duplicated domain rules, remove the duplication rather
  than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization,
  consumers, and persistence together.

## Financial totals contract

- The backend member summary owns mandatory declared GBP totals across all
  categories, including unknown category IDs. Frontends display those fields
  without recalculation or fallback sums.
- Current-term totals include records registered on or after
  `2024-07-09T00:00:00Z`. Historical totals include all records; undated records
  belong only to historical totals.
- Preserve exact decimal amounts and currencies. Do not convert currencies or
  pass amounts through JavaScript `Number`. Missing GBP amounts and unknown
  currencies make totals incomplete; known foreign currencies are excluded from
  GBP amounts without making totals incomplete.
- Preserve declaration counts and distinguish null amounts from zero. Label
  these as declared amounts, not earnings: declarations can include rates and
  benefits rather than money earned.
- Financial semantic changes require explicit user authorization and a description
  of their effects on included records/categories, currency, registration dates,
  missing values, precision, and labels. UI changes and refactoring must preserve
  these rules.

## Frontend coding policy

- Frontend presentation is largely a prototype. UI edits must preserve the financial contract above.

### UI copy scope

- Add only the visible text needed for the requested interaction or data.
  Do not add unrequested subtitles, helper paragraphs, explanatory labels,
  badges, or repeated context to make a feature feel complete.
- Reuse existing wording. Keep required control labels, accessible names,
  error messages, and the financial wording required above.
- Before committing UI changes, review each added visible string against the
  request. Remove optional copy that the user did not request. A component
  example is not permission to copy its explanatory text into a feature.

| Rule | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Omit unrequested visible UI copy. | Review added strings in the diff against the user's request. This is a judgment check; types and automated tests cannot determine whether copy was requested. |

### Client and server

- Use Node.js 24+. From `frontend`, run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` for local
  development. Production uses `npm run build` followed by `node build`.
- Render initial page data through SvelteKit server loads. Keep Rust API access
  and response parsing in `frontend/src/lib/server` and `+page.server.ts`.
- Keep `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` on the server. Browser navigation and data requests
  go through the same-origin SvelteKit application, not directly to the Rust API.
- Pass typed, serializable page models to components. Keep browser APIs and SDK
  initialization in client hooks, event handlers, or `onMount` so SSR stays safe.
- Declare public configuration in `frontend/src/env.ts`. Use `dev` from
  `$app/env` for development-only behavior, including the design-system route.

### PostHog

- Initialize PostHog in `frontend/src/hooks.client.ts`, only outside development
  and when both public PostHog configuration values are present.
- Capture events in feature handlers, once per executed action. Preserve event
  names and property shapes for existing actions. Keep analytics out of shared UI
  components.
- Record metadata such as query length, entity type, and result position rather
  than raw search text or response payloads.
- Use `posthogLogger` for frontend diagnostic logs. Keep client error capture in
  the existing hook instead of adding duplicate exception reports.

### Design system

- Read the [component reference](frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md) and
  [composition recipes](frontend/src/lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md) before adding UI.
  The interactive reference is `/design-system` in development only.
- Import components and types from `frontend/src/lib/ui/index.ts` through the
  appropriate relative path. Load `frontend/src/lib/ui/styles.css` once in the
  root layout.
- Reuse components and typed variants. Use tokens for colors, spacing, and
  focus. Purple identifies MPs, teal identifies funders, and utility icons use
  the muted neutral color.
- Keep page arrangement, URLs, async work, and financial formatting in features.
  Shared UI accepts presentation models. Scope feature CSS to page arrangement
  and caller-authored content rather than component internals.
- Extend reusable patterns in `frontend/src/lib/ui`. Export public additions
  from the barrel, document their contracts, and add a gallery example. Cover
  changed behavior in `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` or feature tests.

### UI verification

- Run `npm run check`, `npm run build`, and the affected Playwright tests from
  `frontend`. Gallery tests use a development server. Production tests use the
  built application.
- Every PR that changes the UI must include desktop screenshots in its
  description. Capture the affected views from the running application on
  the PR branch after completing the changes.
- Upload screenshots as GitHub attachments with `gh pr create --attach` or
  `gh pr edit --attach`. Use a GitHub CLI version that supports this flag. Never
  commit PR screenshots to the repository. Verify that the attachments render
  in the PR description before marking the PR ready for review.


## Git history

- After completing and validating a task, commit its changes on the task's work
  branch, push the branch, and open a pull request against the target branch
  without waiting for a separate request. If the branch already has an open PR,
  update it instead of creating a duplicate.
- Before reporting completion, verify that the remote branch matches local
  `HEAD` and that the open PR targets the intended base and includes that commit.
  Include the PR URL and validation results in the final response.
- If pushing or opening the PR fails, report the blocker and the remaining step.
  Do not describe a local commit alone as completed delivery. Follow explicit
  user instructions to stop before pushing or opening a PR.
- Never commit directly on `main`.
- Keep Git history linear. Rebase feature branches onto the target branch and
  integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits.

| Rule | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Deliver validated changes as a pushed branch with an open PR. | Agent completion check against the remote branch and `gh pr view`; include the verified PR URL in the final response. This is a workflow rule, not an automated gate. CI cannot observe work that was never pushed. |

## Development database migrations

- Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and
  `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with
  `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible <name>`.
- Never change a migration file that existed before the current PR. Treat those
  migrations as immutable, even when they have not been applied locally.
- When a PR's schema design changes, you must edit, consolidate, or remove the
  migrations introduced by that PR. Do not append a corrective migration for an
  obsolete step in the same PR. Before review, the PR must contain only the
  migrations needed for its final schema. Recreate isolated test databases that
  applied a discarded PR migration; do not preserve obsolete steps just to
  satisfy their checksums.
- Do not fold changes into the baseline or put manual schema scripts in
  `db/upgrades`.
- From the repository root, apply migrations with
  `sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, inspect them with
  `sqlx migrate info --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, and revert the
  latest version with
  `sqlx migrate revert --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`.
  Commands read the root `.env`; set `DATABASE_URL` to select another database.
- SQLx owns each migration transaction. Do not add `BEGIN` or `COMMIT` to the
  migration files. Keep each down migration limited to its up migration's changes.
- Test forward upgrades with existing records and the full down/up cycle in an
  isolated database. Preserve imported data when upgrading an existing database.
- The one-time transition from the consolidated baseline requires schema and
  data verification before aligning its checksum. Follow `db/README.md`;
  changing the checksum alone does not apply schema changes.

# Project summary and structure The goal of this project is to make declaration data easy to search, browse and interpret. - `exposed/` contains the rust application and CLI code that powers the project. - `frontend/` contains a simple Svelte application ## Worktree policy - For read-only tasks (investigating, reading, summarizing, or describing code), work on the current branch without creating a worktree. - For tasks that require changing code or other files, use [`worktrunk`](https://worktrunk.dev): - `wt switch --create --base main` - Never modify the primary checkout without explicit permission. ## Exposed coding policy - Follow with strict detail to the existing style of the application. This includes: - Type driven design - Domain modelling and parse-not-validate - Consistent error handling - Service layer abstractions - Interactions with the database must use `sqlx` macros for compile-time query verification. - For Rust changes, read and apply the [Rust domain development skill](.agents/skills/rust-domain-development/SKILL.md). - Before implementation, identify the domain states, invariants, and the type that owns each rule. Parse external values into those types at boundaries and retain typed values internally. - Use one canonical domain enum for each finite vocabulary. Do not duplicate its variants in string allowlists. Use exhaustive matches where behavior depends on a variant. - When a bug exposes duplicated domain rules, remove the duplication rather than synchronizing the copies. Trace changes through producers, serialization, consumers, and persistence together. ## Financial totals contract - The backend member summary owns mandatory declared GBP totals across all categories, including unknown category IDs. Frontends display those fields without recalculation or fallback sums. - Current-term totals include records registered on or after `2024-07-09T00:00:00Z`. Historical totals include all records; undated records belong only to historical totals. - Preserve exact decimal amounts and currencies. Do not convert currencies or pass amounts through JavaScript `Number`. Missing GBP amounts and unknown currencies make totals incomplete; known foreign currencies are excluded from GBP amounts without making totals incomplete. - Preserve declaration counts and distinguish null amounts from zero. Label these as declared amounts, not earnings: declarations can include rates and benefits rather than money earned. - Financial semantic changes require explicit user authorization and a description of their effects on included records/categories, currency, registration dates, missing values, precision, and labels. UI changes and refactoring must preserve these rules. ## Frontend coding policy - Frontend presentation is largely a prototype. UI edits must preserve the financial contract above. ### UI copy scope - Add only the visible text needed for the requested interaction or data. Do not add unrequested subtitles, helper paragraphs, explanatory labels, badges, or repeated context to make a feature feel complete. - Reuse existing wording. Keep required control labels, accessible names, error messages, and the financial wording required above. - Before committing UI changes, review each added visible string against the request. Remove optional copy that the user did not request. A component example is not permission to copy its explanatory text into a feature. | Rule | Enforcement | | --- | --- | | Omit unrequested visible UI copy. | Review added strings in the diff against the user's request. This is a judgment check; types and automated tests cannot determine whether copy was requested. | ### Client and server - Use Node.js 24+. From `frontend`, run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` for local development. Production uses `npm run build` followed by `node build`. - Render initial page data through SvelteKit server loads. Keep Rust API access and response parsing in `frontend/src/lib/server` and `+page.server.ts`. - Keep `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` on the server. Browser navigation and data requests go through the same-origin SvelteKit application, not directly to the Rust API. - Pass typed, serializable page models to components. Keep browser APIs and SDK initialization in client hooks, event handlers, or `onMount` so SSR stays safe. - Declare public configuration in `frontend/src/env.ts`. Use `dev` from `$app/env` for development-only behavior, including the design-system route. ### PostHog - Initialize PostHog in `frontend/src/hooks.client.ts`, only outside development and when both public PostHog configuration values are present. - Capture events in feature handlers, once per executed action. Preserve event names and property shapes for existing actions. Keep analytics out of shared UI components. - Record metadata such as query length, entity type, and result position rather than raw search text or response payloads. - Use `posthogLogger` for frontend diagnostic logs. Keep client error capture in the existing hook instead of adding duplicate exception reports. ### Design system - Read the [component reference](frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md) and [composition recipes](frontend/src/lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md) before adding UI. The interactive reference is `/design-system` in development only. - Import components and types from `frontend/src/lib/ui/index.ts` through the appropriate relative path. Load `frontend/src/lib/ui/styles.css` once in the root layout. - Reuse components and typed variants. Use tokens for colors, spacing, and focus. Purple identifies MPs, teal identifies funders, and utility icons use the muted neutral color. - Keep page arrangement, URLs, async work, and financial formatting in features. Shared UI accepts presentation models. Scope feature CSS to page arrangement and caller-authored content rather than component internals. - Extend reusable patterns in `frontend/src/lib/ui`. Export public additions from the barrel, document their contracts, and add a gallery example. Cover changed behavior in `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` or feature tests. ### UI verification - Run `npm run check`, `npm run build`, and the affected Playwright tests from `frontend`. Gallery tests use a development server. Production tests use the built application. - Every PR that changes the UI must include desktop screenshots in its description. Capture the affected views from the running application on the PR branch after completing the changes. - Upload screenshots as GitHub attachments with `gh pr create --attach` or `gh pr edit --attach`. Use a GitHub CLI version that supports this flag. Never commit PR screenshots to the repository. Verify that the attachments render in the PR description before marking the PR ready for review. ## Git history - After completing and validating a task, commit its changes on the task's work branch, push the branch, and open a pull request against the target branch without waiting for a separate request. If the branch already has an open PR, update it instead of creating a duplicate. - Before reporting completion, verify that the remote branch matches local `HEAD` and that the open PR targets the intended base and includes that commit. Include the PR URL and validation results in the final response. - If pushing or opening the PR fails, report the blocker and the remaining step. Do not describe a local commit alone as completed delivery. Follow explicit user instructions to stop before pushing or opening a PR. - Never commit directly on `main`. - Keep Git history linear. Rebase feature branches onto the target branch and integrate changes with a fast-forward or squash; do not create merge commits. | Rule | Enforcement | | --- | --- | | Deliver validated changes as a pushed branch with an open PR. | Agent completion check against the remote branch and `gh pr view`; include the verified PR URL in the final response. This is a workflow rule, not an automated gate. CI cannot observe work that was never pushed. | ## Development database migrations - Keep schema changes in `db/migrations` as SQLx versioned `.up.sql` and `.down.sql` pairs. From the repository root, create a pair with `sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible `. - Never change a migration file that existed before the current PR. Treat those migrations as immutable, even when they have not been applied locally. - When a PR's schema design changes, you must edit, consolidate, or remove the migrations introduced by that PR. Do not append a corrective migration for an obsolete step in the same PR. Before review, the PR must contain only the migrations needed for its final schema. Recreate isolated test databases that applied a discarded PR migration; do not preserve obsolete steps just to satisfy their checksums. - Do not fold changes into the baseline or put manual schema scripts in `db/upgrades`. - From the repository root, apply migrations with `sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, inspect them with `sqlx migrate info --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`, and revert the latest version with `sqlx migrate revert --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations`. Commands read the root `.env`; set `DATABASE_URL` to select another database. - SQLx owns each migration transaction. Do not add `BEGIN` or `COMMIT` to the migration files. Keep each down migration limited to its up migration's changes. - Test forward upgrades with existing records and the full down/up cycle in an isolated database. Preserve imported data when upgrading an existing database. - The one-time transition from the consolidated baseline requires schema and data verification before aligning its checksum. Follow `db/README.md`; changing the checksum alone does not apply schema changes. # Monthly updates design Use /tmp/monthly-design-astra.md as the base sketch. All three candidates recommend a dedicated updates service and nonfinancial repository projection. The service exposes one current-month operation; RegistrationMonth owns UTC half-open boundaries. Query one snapshot across every category, canonicalize funders, retain no-entry MPs, deduplicate declaration IDs per entity, return all rows ordered latest registration descending then exact name then ID. Share exhaustive FunderKind::is_individual with rankings. Keep financial totals unchanged. Frontend /updates uses a server-only parser and SSR load. Show Updates, formatted UTC month, MPs and Companies sections, entity profile links, declaration counts and latest dates. Reuse ResultRow and existing tokens. Add a landing-page Updates link, no new explanatory copy. No amounts, pagination, or month picker. The nonzero EntityUpdate count from Astra prevents an empty entity row. Keep optional member party/constituency context out of this first view to reduce copy and query payload. HTTP captures one UTC clock instant and passes it into UpdatesService::updates(now); service constructs the typed month. Tests supply an explicit instant. Rejected extending RankingsService because it couples activity with financial ranking rules. Rejected SQL aggregation because it duplicates classification and hides count policy from domain tests. Rubric scores by parent, completeness/invariants/interface/isolation/testability. Astra 5/5/5/5/5. Sol 5/5/4/5/5. Luna 5/4/5/5/4. All designs converge; Astra gives the clearest exact ordering and nonzero shape. Cross-judge agrees Astra base, scoring Astra 25, Sol 24, Luna 21. Adopt Sol explicit service instant supplied once by HTTP for deterministic full-service tests, replacing current_month() with updates(now). Also validate month boundaries and row membership in frontend parser. Parent accepts both grafts. # Monthly updates: dedicated activity projection ## Problem and grounding `rankings` has useful integration patterns but the wrong data contract for updates. Its service loads declarations since the parliament boundary, applies exact financial totals, limits every board to ten, and includes funders only for DonationSupport. Its repository selects all financial entry columns and parses currencies and categories into `MemberDeclaration`; canonical identity comes from `funder_alias_groups`, root `funders`, and `funder_group_names`. Its HTTP adapter formats identities; the frontend server parser enforces ten entries and a financial total. Reusing that operation would silently lose relevant records or import irrelevant financial validation. `AppState` currently injects three services. The Svelte route uses a server load, private API origin, typed page data, and AppShell. AppShell has no primary navigation; its footer contains Methodology and development-only Design system. Updates should integrate through the same server-load pattern and an Updates navigation link without reworking the shell. ## Usage (written before types) Backend HTTP handler: ```rust let updates = state.updates_service.current_month().await?; Ok(ApiSuccess::new(StatusCode::OK, UpdatesResponse::from(updates))) ``` Frontend server load: ```ts return { updates: await loadUpdates(fetch, request.signal, origin), error: null }; // Catch maps to existing-style user-facing error; no client API origin. ``` Page: ```svelte

Updates

 ``` Each returned section contains every qualifying identity, in final display order. Callers do not select a month, apply a cutoff, classify funders, deduplicate, sort, paginate, calculate totals, or join data. ## Shape Choose a dedicated `updates` model, repository projection, and application service. Keep existing rankings public API unchanged. Reuse canonical identity resolution SQL join shape and the existing MemberId, FunderId and FunderKind types, not ranking financial objects. The interface is one operation that hides calendar selection, scope, canonicalization, distinct counting and ordering. ```rust // domain/models/updates.rs pub struct RegistrationMonth { start: DateTime, end: DateTime } impl RegistrationMonth { // Private fields; start is UTC day 1 midnight, end the following month's start. pub fn containing(now: DateTime) -> Self { todo!() } pub fn start(&self) -> DateTime { todo!() } pub fn end(&self) -> DateTime { todo!() } } pub struct UpdatedMember { pub id: MemberId, pub name: String } pub struct UpdatedCompany { pub id: FunderId, pub name: String } pub struct EntityUpdate { pub identity: I, pub declaration_count: NonZeroUsize, pub latest_registration: DateTime, } pub struct MonthlyUpdates { pub month: RegistrationMonth, pub members: Vec>, pub companies: Vec>, } // Repository-facing domain facts, not wire or database rows. pub struct UpdateDeclaration { pub source_id: i32, pub registered_at: DateTime, pub member: UpdatedMember, pub funders: Vec, } pub struct UpdateFunder { pub id: FunderId, pub name: String, pub kind: FunderKind } // domain/repositories/updates.rs pub trait UpdatesRepo: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static { fn declarations(&self, month: &RegistrationMonth) -> impl Future, UpdatesError>> + Send; } // domain/services/updates.rs pub trait UpdatesService: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static { fn current_month(&self) -> impl Future> + Send; } pub struct Service { repo: R } impl Service { pub fn new(repo: R) -> Self { todo!() } // Service samples Utc::now() once and derives one month before fetching. // Pure summarization is independently testable with a supplied month and facts. } fn summarize(month: RegistrationMonth, declarations: Vec) -> MonthlyUpdates { todo!() } ``` Do not create a shared generic identity abstraction merely to remove two small names-plus-ID structs. Member and funder IDs remain distinct internally; HTTP alone serializes them as strings. `outbound/updates.rs` implements the repository with one `sqlx::query!` statement: declarations JOIN members, LEFT JOIN funding_entries, LEFT JOIN funder_alias_groups, LEFT JOIN canonical root funders, LEFT JOIN funder_group_names. Select only declaration ID, registration date, member identity, canonical funder ID/name/kind. Filter `d.registration_date >= $1 AND d.registration_date < $2`; no category predicate, no amount/currency predicates, no LIMIT. Preserve declaration rows with no funding entries or no identified funder, because their MP still qualifies. Reconstruct one fact per declaration using stable source-ID ordering. Parse stored FunderKind through its canonical parser; unknown classification is NotSpecified only when absent, matching existing rankings behavior. Malformed nonempty values remain errors. Add `FunderKind::is_individual()` with an exhaustive match. Both rankings and updates use this method to distinguish individual from all other kinds. This makes the existing companies convention have one owner without inventing a second enum or a synchronized string allowlist. The method's name describes classification rather than incorrectly declaring every organization legally a company. Replace only rankings' classification branch, preserving financial semantics. `inbound/http/handlers/updates.rs` defines transport-only `UpdatesResponse`: `month_start`, `month_end`, `members`, `companies`; each row has `id`, `name`, `declaration_count`, `latest_registration`. Map nonzero domain count to JSON integer. Add `U: UpdatesService` and `updates_service: Arc` to AppState and route wiring, following the existing explicit dependency pattern. This costs generic-parameter propagation but avoids coupling updates availability to a rankings service. Frontend `lib/server/updates.ts` owns response parsing and fetch timeout; `lib/updates.ts` owns serializable page models and display formatting; `routes/updates/+page.server.ts` owns initial server fetch; `routes/updates/+page.svelte` owns arrangement. Parser validates timestamp shape, IDs, positive safe integer counts and unique identities within each section. It accepts arrays longer than ten. Preserve backend order. No financial helpers or decimal conversion are needed. Display dates using UTC and use existing `/members/{id}` and `/funders/{canonical-id}` destinations. Reuse ResultRow, SectionHeading and Notice; native lists and feature-authored counts/date content need no new shared component. Add only Updates, month, MPs, Companies, counts, dates, required error/empty wording and navigation text; no explanatory subtitles or badges. ## Ownership and exact rules RegistrationMonth alone owns UTC calendar arithmetic, including December rollover and leap years. Current month is sampled once per request on the backend and sent to the frontend; browser time zones and import timestamps cannot change membership. Start is inclusive, next month start exclusive; null registration dates never qualify. Future-dated records within the current month qualify, because the rule is month membership rather than month-to-now. All source category IDs qualify, including unknown IDs. Amounts, currency, missing amounts and payment types do not influence this feature. Repository owns storage mapping and canonical aliases. Canonical root determines ID and kind, preferred group name determines display name, root name is fallback. Service owns activity aggregation and ordering. Track source declaration IDs per entity to count each source declaration once. Multiple funding entries, repeated occurrences and aliases resolving to one canonical group contribute one count to that company. One declaration involving several companies contributes once to each. Members count declarations even without a company. Individual canonical roots are excluded only from Companies, never from their recipient MP's activity. After grouping, sort each section by latest registration descending, then exact stored display name ascending, then numeric MemberId or UUID bytes ascending. Use Rust ordering to avoid database collation/environment differences. All identities are retained. EntityUpdate uses a nonzero count and nonoptional date because rows cannot exist without at least one qualifying declaration. No ranking, financial total or coverage state is exposed. ## Alternatives considered 1. Extend RankingsService with updates and reuse ranking_declarations(start).
